_comment: Planning Plan generator. Authored at the Phase 2 assessability floor; meta-family that covers the SSP itself (PL-2), Rules of Behavior (PL-4), security / privacy architectures (PL-8), baseline selection (PL-10), and baseline tailoring (PL-11). Pairs with every other family — the SSP it documents is the umbrella that incorporates each family plan; pairs especially with CA (PL-2 SSP feeds CA-2 assessment + CA-6 authorization), RA (PL-10 / PL-11 baseline selection responds to RA-2 categorization), and PS (PL-4 RoB pairs with PS-6 access agreements).
title: Planning Plan
description: Documents how the system's planning artifacts — System Security Plan (SSP), Rules of Behavior, security and privacy architectures, baseline selection, and baseline tailoring — are governed across creation, review, change-control, and integration with the broader RMF package. Covers the controls of the PL family in NIST SP 800-53 r5 and aligns with NIST SP 800-37 r2 (RMF), NIST SP 800-160 v1 r1 (Engineering Trustworthy Secure Systems), NIST SP 800-18 r1 (Guide for Developing Security Plans), FIPS 199 / 200 (baseline selection), and CNSSI 1253 (overlays for national-security systems).
intro_template:
This Planning Plan documents the planning approach for {system_name}. It establishes the practices, cadences, and roles used to author and maintain the SSP, draft and update Rules of Behavior, document security and privacy architectures, select control baselines per FIPS 199 / 200, and apply tailoring decisions through overlays and supplements.

The scope covers SSP management per PL-2, Rules of Behavior per PL-4, security and privacy architectures per PL-8, baseline selection per PL-10, and baseline tailoring per PL-11 within the {system_name} authorization boundary. The plan is consistent with NIST SP 800-53 r5 (Planning family), NIST SP 800-18 r1 (Guide for Developing Security Plans), and NIST SP 800-37 r2 (Risk Management Framework).
approach_template:
{system_name} maintains its System Security Plan at {ssp_location} under the ownership of {ssp_owner_role}. The Rules of Behavior are at {rob_location} and are reaffirmed by personnel on the cadence in §4.3. The security and privacy architectures are at {architecture_location} with change-control routed through {architecture_governance_role}. The baseline selected per FIPS 199 / 200 categorization is {selected_baseline_summary}; tailoring decisions and overlays applied are documented at {tailoring_register_location}.

Additional details on SSP management, Rules of Behavior, security architecture, baseline selection, and baseline tailoring are captured in the sub-sections below.
continuous_monitoring_template: Planning-artifact currency for {system_name} is tracked through the metrics in §6.1 (SSP review cycle adherence, RoB acknowledgment-completion rate, architecture-currency rate, baseline-tailoring-decision currency, control-supplement / removal change rate). Planning artifacts are reviewed on the cadence in §6.2; significant changes (per CM-4) trigger immediate updates rather than waiting for the next periodic cycle. The SSP and supporting plans surface to the AO at the cadence required by the ATO conditions.
integration_template: This Planning Plan does not stand alone — it documents *how* the meta-artifacts that bind every other family plan are governed. The CA family consumes the SSP for CA-2 assessment and CA-6 authorization decisions; the RA family supplies the FIPS 199 categorization that drives PL-10 baseline selection; the CM family routes architecture / SSP changes through CM-3 change control; the PS family pairs PL-4 Rules of Behavior with PS-6 access agreements; every family plan referenced in this RMF package is itself a child artifact under the SSP. The following cross-references identify the specific artifacts and locations where PL-related content is exchanged with other RMF deliverables.

questions.help: How often the SSP is reviewed (typical: 'Annual + on significant change per CM-4').

questions.help: Per PL-4(1) — restrictions on disclosing system / org information via social media. What may not be disclosed (system identifiers, technical details, project codes, classified or CUI material).

family_questions.label: Security and Privacy Architecture (PL-8)

questions.help: How often the architecture document is reviewed for currency. Per NIST SP 800-160 v1 r1.

Initial threat model maintained; updated on major change
Threat model not formally maintained (with POA&M)

questions.label: Privacy-architecture maturity

glossary.definition: A short document capturing an architecture-significant decision, its context, and consequences. Common evidence vehicle for PL-8 and SA-8 principle application.
Per PL-10, the starting set of controls applicable to a system based on FIPS 199 categorization. Drawn from NIST SP 800-53B (Low / Moderate / High) or equivalent (FedRAMP, CNSSI 1253).
Per FIPS 199, the assignment of Low / Moderate / High impact ratings to a system based on confidentiality, integrity, and availability impacts. Drives PL-10 baseline selection. Reference RA-2.

Committee on National Security Systems Instruction 1253 — categorization and control-selection guidance for national-security systems. Provides separate confidentiality / integrity / availability baselines plus classified overlays.
Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service — DoD's authoritative tool for managing RMF packages including the SSP.
Federal Information Processing Standard 199 — Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems. Defines the C / I / A impact-level framework.
Federal Information Processing Standard 200 — Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems. Mandates categorization-driven baseline selection.
Per FIPS 199, the highest impact level across all information types within a system. The system inherits this level as its overall categorization.

Per NIST SP 800-53B § 2.4, a fully specified set of controls, control enhancements, and supplemental guidance derived from baseline controls and tailored to address specific protection needs (privacy, classified, ICS, etc.).
Per PL-4, a set of rules describing user obligations and acceptable use of system resources. Often co-administered with PS-6 access agreements.
Per NIST SP 800-37 r2 § 3.6 and CM-4, a change that, alone or in combination with other changes, is likely to affect the security state of the system. Triggers PL-2 SSP update.
System Security Plan — the formal document that describes the system, its categorization, applicable controls, and how each control is implemented. Subject of PL-2.

Per NIST SP 800-37 r2 § 3.3 and PL-11, the process of modifying a baseline by applying overlays, scoping considerations, parameter selections, control supplements, and risk-based decisions to fit a specific system context.
A structured analysis of system threats, vulnerabilities, and countermeasures. Per PL-8 and SA-11(2). Common methodologies: STRIDE, PASTA, attack trees.
